description: Ownership of every legacy table, its target tables, owned columns and units; a unit of write authority is one target table.

ruleSteps.1: Entity owner: the service that owns the entity owns its table.
ruleSteps.2: Membership and permission tables go to identity.
ruleSteps.3: Other services keep an id plus an event-fed projection.
ruleSteps.5: Anything else goes on the decision list.

conventions.owner: A service folder name, split (owners per target), decision-list, retired, or migration (OPT-2 coordination state).

columnPolicy.whole-table: The target owns every live column of the legacy table; ownedColumns lists the static set.

rowIdentity.multiset: Rows match on their full canonical encoding; the target stores legacy_row_hash and an occurrence number.

tenantResolution.siteID: tenantIdForSite(siteID); the column is NOT NULL.
tenantResolution.siteID-or-umbrella: tenantIdForSite(siteID), or the umbrella tenant with an orphan flag when siteID is null or names no site.
tenantResolution.parent:<table>: The parent row's tenant through tenantParent.join; a row with no parent, or parents in several tenants, loads under the umbrella tenant as an orphan.
tenantResolution.program_site: synthetic.program_site maps the Program_<id> schema to its siteID, then tenantIdForSite; the fold adds legacy_program_id.

conventions.liveCatalog: false only for a table the pinned code drops; fixture tables exist after legacy-fixtures/load-fixtures.sh.
conventions.programN: Program_N stands for each of Program_1 and Program_2, which hold the same table set.

countNotes.withSiteIdStatic: Counts tcontentfilemetadata, whose siteID comes from the beanORMVersioned base, and tremotepointer, which an install creates lazily, so a fresh live catalog shows 54.
countNotes.noPrimaryKeyAfterMigrations: tsettings gains its key in core/mura/dbUpdates/6.1.cfm:120-122 and tglobals is retired, leaving 8 keyless live tables.

units.notes: Target-only survey task ledger, written through seam 2 by the entry points that write surveys.survey_schedule and adopted or cancelled in the transition that moves the surveys units, so it shares that unit's group.

tables.notes: Form-builder tables generated at runtime from component strings; every live table named fb_* matches this entry.
Reverse-projector checkpoint that only the migration service writes inside the legacy database; it is coordination state and never migrates.
It links approval chains to approving groups, which is workflow configuration rather than a user-to-group membership, so step 2 does not apply and group names are read by projection.
